title: The Farewell
dek: With Commish gone and nobody answering, the man who had run the forums for four years wrote an open letter, resigned, and promised the community he wasn't leaving it. Then the old chat room went dark, and the forums followed.
stats: Greek Wizard ran the forums unpaid
forum users who needed a new home
logTitle: How it ended, and how it didn't

chapters.title: The Letter to The Commish
text: Commish had gone offline even on ICQ, so Greek Wizard wrote to him in public. They had built the community together in October 2002. GW had run the forums for four years for little more than a few tickets, and he was done. He resigned as Administrator with 30 days' notice, landing on October 22: four years to the day after the smallball.org domain was bought.

He gave Commish three outcomes: leave the forums running with nobody watching, let GW appoint a replacement, or let the domain lapse. To the community he wrote that it might look like he was abandoning them too, and that the opposite was true.
quotes: You just have to trust me on this

chapters.title: The Q&A
text: GW opened a thread for replies and answered the obvious questions. Copy anything you want to keep, especially tickets sitting in private messages. Registrations would stop. He was stepping down as admin, not leaving SmallBall.

Then he thanked the moderators one by one: Beaner, the good cop to his bad cop; Tim's Dodgers; TNT1, great guy with awesome morals; mlthmp, quiet, yet people listen; and the former mods, from LadyHwk and NMShooter to Fred, the shortest-serving Global Mod, for a reason.
quotes: I am not leaving the Smallball Community
An Admin really does nothing anyways, i should know, I am one
Greek Wizard, quoting an old line

chapters.title: The goodbyes pour in
chapters.text: Over a hundred replies in a few days. humdrums stands up and claps alone. TThomp says GW's thank-you list reads like a who's who. ERG says he practically grew up on these forums. BP, of course, has heard soccer is coming out in November. Tim's Dodgers has to remind everyone it's a goodbye thread.
quotes: A new community will pop up, mark my words.
You have ruled this forum with an iron fist, but mostly a fair iron fist
this is where the legends of smallball become dust in the wind

chapters.title: Only the forums
chapters.text: GW clears up the panic: only smallball.org, the forums and the Hall of Fame, is going down. The game itself should stay online for months, maybe longer. Keep training. Just don't count on tickets arriving.

chapters.title: Something up his sleeve
chapters.text: Beaner calls it one of the best threads ever, pulling in people who never post. Word spreads that GW and Chexx are building something new, and the mood turns from sad to curious.

chapters.title: A bigger server
chapters.text: GW moves the new site to a server four times the size of smallball.org's and says they plan to do better than the old forums ever did.

chapters.title: RIP OSBC
text: The Official SmallBall Chat shuts down a week early. It had been open since New Year's Eve 2003.

chspogo remembers saying hi to Slip at 2 am and waiting half an hour for no answer. MaluBro07 remembers summer freerolls, the Userleague 101 Game Series, and de-hammering Money, Slip and Smith. Beaner calls it the end of an era.
quotes: What will I be known for except the guy that is ALWAYS in the chat?

chapters.title: World Sports Forums
chapters.text: GW reports the new site is in its final stages. It was planned because 4,500 forum users would have had nowhere to go if smallball.org wasn't renewed. Talk turns to poker nights.

chapters.title: Pulling the plug
chapters.text: On New Year's Eve, Greek Wizard posts the final message on the old forums. The Commish had his chance to respond and didn't, so GW, who made the first post there, makes the last.

chapters.title: The community lives
chapters.text: By the next summer the community had a home again at smallball.org, kept going by jon2s and Greek Wizard. That's where Commish found it when he came back.
